dedupe_keys.name: lacor hospital energy community power data st mary s hospital lacor gulu uganda 2022

description: This data set records how electricity is produced and used at St. Mary's Hospital Lacor in Gulu, northern Uganda, one of the largest private non-profit hospitals in the country, which runs as a small energy community with its own solar panels and a diesel back-up generator. The producers are Alex Felice of the Vrije Universiteit Brussel and Jacopo Barbieri of the hospital. Coverage is almost six months, from 1 May to 25 October 2022, at five-minute resolution. The series give solar PV production, the total load of the hospital community, the output of the back-up diesel generator and the consumption of the sterilisation machine, which is one of the largest single loads. The file is available as a free XLSX download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: grid imports and outage times are not listed as separate variables in the description, there is no documentation of meters or data gaps, and it covers one site. Simulation uses: sizing solar, battery and generator systems for hospitals, modelling how a health facility rides through grid outages, and studying the electricity demand of clinical services in low-income settings. Related records: the Caribbean smart hospitals case (case_study-caribbean-smart-hospitals) covers energy and climate retrofits of health facilities, and the Jinja oxygen storage trial (data-jinja-oxygen-storage-power-outages) measures how outages affect oxygen supply.
